note: Built by backend/pipeline/site_physics.py from NASA LRO (LOLA, Diviner) products and JPL Horizons; every field names its source. See backend/data/SOURCES.md.

illum.label: LOLA illumination (NASA LRO)
illum.title: LRO LOLA average solar illumination, south pole (Mazarico et al. 2011 method; PDS product AVGVISIB_*_201608)

earth.label: LOLA Earth visibility (NASA LRO)
earth.title: LRO LOLA average Earth visibility, south pole (PDS product AVGVISIB_*_201608_EARTH)

psr.label: LOLA shadow map (NASA LRO)
psr.title: LRO LOLA permanently shadowed regions, south pole (PDS product LPSR_*_201608)

slope.label: LOLA slope (NASA LRO)
slope.title: LRO LOLA gridded slope, south pole (PDS LDSM_85S_40M, LDSM_75S_120M)

diviner.label: Diviner temperatures (NASA LRO)
diviner.title: LRO Diviner South Polar Resource Product (Paige et al. 2010, Science 330:479; PDS LRO-L-DLRE-5-PRP-V2.0)

horizons.label: JPL Horizons + LOLA terrain
horizons.title: JPL Horizons Sun and Earth positions (hourly, 2026) against the LOLA terrain horizon (LDEM_75S_120M), computed by this pipeline

artemis2024.label: NASA, Oct 2024
artemis2024.title: NASA Provides Update on Artemis III Moon Landing Regions (Oct 2024)

artemis2022.label: NASA, Aug 2022
artemis2022.title: NASA Identifies Candidate Regions for Landing Next Americans on Moon (Aug 2022)

criteria.label: NASA, LPSC 2026
criteria.title: George et al., Artemis III site selection update: downselection from thirteen to nine candidate regions (NASA NTRS 20250011660)

lroc.label: LROC NAC mosaics
lroc.title: LROC NAC low-Sun controlled mosaics of the Artemis III candidate regions (Henriksen et al. 2023); centre from the product name

regionmap.label: NASA region map
regionmap.title: Position read off NASA's map of the 9 regions (NTRS 20250011660, Image 1), georeferenced on 6 LROC centres; about +/-5 km

viper.label: NASA VIPER
viper.title: NASA VIPER mission overview: top speed 0.72 km/h (0.45 mph); drives on slopes up to 15 deg (NASA, VIPER lunar operations)

items.label: Power
items.why: Solar illumination for the whole surface stay

items.label: Talk to Earth
items.why: Direct-to-Earth radio: more Earth visibility is preferred

items.label: Ice access
items.why: Close enough to permanently shadowed ground for a moonwalk or a drive

items.label: Safe landing
items.why: Low slopes for a safe landing

sunlight_pct.basis: average over 18.6 years (hourly) at the best-lit spot flatter than 10 deg within 1 km; range: 10th percentile to the best nearby

longest_dark_h.basis: longest stretch in 2026 with no part of the Sun above the LOLA terrain horizon, seen from 2 m up at the spot

earth_pct.basis: average over 18.6 years at the spot (any part of Earth's disc in view); range over the area (10th-90th percentile)

slope_deg.basis: mean slope within 250 m of the spot; range over the area (10th-90th percentile)

psr_km.basis: straight-line distance to the nearest permanently shadowed ground

ice_km.basis: straight-line distance to the nearest ground cold enough (Diviner) for water ice to last right at the surface; range starts at ice buried under at most 1 m. Where ice CAN last, not a detection

temp_c.basis: Diviner: yearly average to yearly maximum surface temperature at the spot

check.note: 2026 only (JPL Horizons vs the LOLA horizon): a cross-check of the 18.6-year LOLA averages

rover_basis.basis: hours one way to the ice: the straight-line distance at NASA VIPER's top speed (0.72 km/h), slower on slopes (half speed at 15 deg, VIPER's design limit)
